tasks.short: Monitor promotion results and judge whether campaigns justify their costs.

steps.what: Export promotion responses and attributed sales.
Collect media spend, supplier charges, discounts, and campaign budget.
Match campaign identifiers and resolve missing costs or inconsistent reporting periods.
Calculate response rates, acquisition costs, contribution, and budget variance.
Judge cost effectiveness and recommend continuing, changing, or stopping the promotion.
Send the scorecard and recommendation to campaign stakeholders.

tasks.design: Configure feeds from {ADS}, {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, {CRM}, and {ERP}; use a mapping job on {DATA_PLATFORM} to reconcile campaign identifiers and reporting periods. A {BI} scorecard exposes source totals, missing costs, attribution assumptions, and approved metrics, while {WORKFLOW} routes exceptions and distributes the manager's recommendation. Spending changes remain separate approval actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Campaign identifiers, cost timing, and attribution definitions differ across systems. Existing reports often cover only one channel.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors and dashboard features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding makes the remaining mapping and reconciliation code cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Attributed sales do not establish incremental sales. Returns, delayed conversions, overlapping promotions, and incomplete margin data can change the conclusion.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether an apparent gain reflects real customer demand, discount subsidy, seasonality, or a weak comparison.

ambition.what: Daily pause-or-continue recommendations for active promotions with sufficiently fresh conversion and cost data.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling reports to investigating weak promotions and designing better comparisons. No spending authority changes automatically; faster recommendations go to the existing budget holder.

reach.task: Design a holdout test for promotion incrementality.
reach.learn: Comparison groups, sample size, uncertainty, and the difference between attribution and causation.

reach.task: Compare promotion contribution across the campaign portfolio.
reach.learn: Contribution margins, commercial constraints, and portfolio tradeoffs.

evidence.claim: Configured connectors and reporting tools can standardise channel data and automate marketing reports.
Marketing automation can report campaign responses and support questions about campaign data.
Identifier reconciliation and metric calculations can use deterministic rules; causal interpretation still requires judgement.

assumptions: This describes a company with channel reports and financial records, joined partly through a workbook.
Time shares are illustrative task shares, not measured customer savings.
Structured inputs support substantial automation despite limited rule coverage for the final commercial judgement.
Build ranges cover an initial campaign family and existing connectors; shared foundations can support the other tasks.
GDPR applies to identifiable customer data. Aggregate reporting should be preferred where sufficient.
unknowns: Which systems expose usable connectors or exports?
Are campaign identifiers shared across sales, media spend, and supplier charges?
Are contribution margins, returns, and discount costs available at the required level?
What conversion delay makes daily recommendations meaningful?
Who approves metric definitions and spending changes?
Will employee-level reporting require consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which reconciliation checks catch missing costs without creating excessive false alarms?
Which campaigns support credible holdout or geographic comparisons?
How much report latency remains after connectors are configured?
new_work: Review unmatched campaign identifiers and late supplier charges.
Maintain metric definitions, cost allocations, and attribution windows.
Monitor connector failures and source schema changes.
Periodically compare attributed returns with experimental evidence.

tasks.short: Represent the organisation at trade association meetings and promote relevant products.

steps.what: Arrange attendance and confirm the association agenda.
Prepare talking points and supporting product material for the audience.

loop.input: Meeting agenda, approved product facts, and permitted association history.
loop.output: Source-linked talking points and suggested questions in a fixed meeting brief.
loop.check: Check every factual claim against approved records; flag unsupported claims and commitments for removal.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; use the standard brief template if validation fails.
loop.why_not_simpler: Audience-specific emphasis requires interpreting agenda language; templates still provide the structure and facts.

steps.what: Approve talking points and limits on commercial commitments.
Discuss member needs, explain products, and build relationships at the meeting.
Record useful contacts, member needs, and promised actions.
Send promised information and arrange the next conversation.

tasks.design: Use {CALENDAR} and {WORKFLOW} for attendance logistics, then combine approved facts from {DOCS} with permitted history from {CRM} in a bounded brief generator. The manager approves the brief, conducts the meeting, and records commitments through a short {CRM} form. Approved templates prepare follow-up messages in {EMAIL}, with a person approving each send.
tasks.previous_blocker: The valuable work happens through live relationships. Preparation and follow-up were small, scattered activities that were rarely separated from the meeting itself.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling, forms, and message templates handle the routine work. A bounded drafting loop can adapt approved facts to an unfamiliar agenda.
tasks.still_hard: Reading the room, handling disagreement, recognising buying signals, and making credible commitments remain personal work.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, hear unstated concerns, and decide when promoting a product would damage the relationship.

ambition.what: A quarterly association member-needs briefing built from reviewed meeting observations.

tasks.altitude: Most time still goes to meetings and relationships, with shorter preparation and fewer lost promises. No new commercial commitment rights are assumed.

reach.learn: Stakeholder interests, reputational sensitivities, and public positioning.

reach.task: Turn recurring member concerns into research questions.
reach.learn: Qualitative coding and the limits of drawing conclusions from informal conversations.

evidence.claim: Branded content drafting is an available capability, although the digest does not establish association-briefing quality.
Scheduling, structured contact forms, and approved message templates can reduce meeting administration.
Most value in association representation comes from human conversation and judgement.

assumptions: The manager normally represents the organisation in person and has access to approved product material.
The meeting remains the largest time share; preparation savings do not imply large overall savings.
The manager can approve ordinary talking points within existing delegated authority.
Live human speech has no additional automated approval gate; prepared claims and delegated limits guide it.
Contact records and follow-up must meet GDPR and applicable ePrivacy and national rules; attendance alone is not marketing consent.
Build ranges assume existing accounts and approved document access; consultation under national rules is included if required.
unknowns: Which commitments can the manager make without further approval?
Where are approved product claims and association history maintained?
What follow-up have members requested or permitted?
Who would use a recurring member-needs briefing?
Are any proposed contact-record changes subject to employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Does an agenda-specific brief improve preparation enough to justify a drafting loop?
Which contact fields capture commitments without encouraging unnecessary personal data collection?
How can association observations be reported without implying a representative market sample?
new_work: Check generated briefs for unsupported claims and unsuitable emphasis.
Keep approved product facts and commitment limits current.
Review recipients, permissions, attachments, and promises before follow-up sends.
Remove stale contact information and close completed commitments.

tasks.short: Design and evaluate surveys, polls, and other methods for collecting useful marketing data.

steps.what: Agree the business question, target population, and decision the research should support.
Review previous questionnaires, findings, and available collection methods.
Choose collection method, sampling approach, response burden, and data safeguards.
Draft questions, answer options, routing, and respondent instructions.

loop.input: Research protocol, approved question bank, reading level, and permitted data fields.
loop.output: Structured questionnaire with question purposes, answer options, routing, and instructions.
loop.check: Validate routing, required fields, permitted data, duplicate questions, and scale consistency; a person checks wording and bias.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; return unresolved items to the manager and reuse approved questions where possible.
loop.why_not_simpler: Approved questions cover recurring needs; novel research questions still require context-specific wording.

steps.what: Pilot the questionnaire and observe misunderstanding, missing options, and completion difficulty.
Revise the method and approve the questionnaire for collection.

tasks.design: Create a searchable method library and versioned question bank in {DOCS}, with a structured research brief in {WORKFLOW}. A questionnaire generator reuses approved questions and uses a bounded loop for new wording, while deterministic checks validate routing, scales, and permitted fields. The manager chooses the method, conducts the pilot, and approves the collection pack.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier questionnaires were difficult to find and reuse. Software could build forms but could not establish whether the questions answered the business problem.
tasks.enabler_now: Search, versioned templates, and deterministic questionnaire checks are established capabilities. Bounded drafting can reduce the effort of adapting wording to a new research brief.
tasks.still_hard: Coverage bias, nonresponse, leading questions, and weak sampling can produce polished but misleading research. Pilot findings require interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Choose an answerable question, challenge the proposed sample, and notice when respondents interpret a question differently.

ambition.what: A pilot-tested questionnaire kit for local event teams measuring attendee needs.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward research framing, pilot observation, and methodological review. The manager gains reusable research capacity; approval rights remain as delegated today.

reach.task: Design a defensible sample and analyse nonresponse.
reach.learn: Sampling frames, precision, weighting, and limits on generalisation.

reach.task: Review questionnaire wording for clarity and consistency.
reach.learn: Plain language, neutral phrasing, accessibility, and consistent response scales.

evidence.claim: Versioned question banks, reusable templates, and routing checks can be implemented without autonomous agents.
Drafting assistance does not establish sampling validity or remove the need for respondent pilots.
The digest supplies no direct product evidence or documented case for survey-method design.

assumptions: This task ends at an approved collection method and questionnaire; full survey fieldwork is separate.
Previous research is held mainly as documents, with methodology decisions discussed in meetings.
Document-heavy inputs support drafting assistance, while low rule coverage keeps method selection human.
GDPR requires a lawful basis, suitable information, data minimisation, and retention controls for personal data.
The pilot gate approves the participant-facing material and permitted fields before respondents see them.
Access and consultation ranges include privacy review and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Who has authority to approve the research method and participant-facing material?
Is there a reusable question bank with known wording and scale provenance?
Which populations and sampling frames are available?
Will questionnaires collect sensitive data or employee responses?
Which collection tools and accessibility requirements must the output support?
What national consultation requirements apply to employee research?
research_questions: Which recurring questions can be reused unchanged?
How reliably do automated checks identify broken routing and inconsistent scales?
Which pilot observations predict misunderstanding during wider collection?
What review effort remains after a generated questionnaire passes structural checks?
new_work: Curate question provenance, approved wording, and known limitations.
Review new wording for bias, ambiguity, and unnecessary personal data.
Maintain routing validators and output templates.
Version protocols and record why pilot findings changed the design.

tasks.short: Contact organisations to explain relevant services and facilities and arrange useful next steps.

steps.what: Select relevant organisations and check contact history and permitted contact routes.
Prepare relevant service details, facility information, and introductory material.
Send an introduction explaining relevance and inviting a conversation.
Explore needs, explain services and facilities, and answer questions.
Record needs, objections, permissions, and agreed next actions.
Send requested information or arrange a service visit.

tasks.design: Configure a contact view in {CRM} with service-fit filters, contact history, and suppression checks. A deterministic generator assembles approved service and facility facts from {DOCS}, while {WORKFLOW} prepares introductions and follow-up through {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}. A person approves outbound messages and conducts the needs conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service facts, relationship history, and contact permissions were scattered. The conversation itself cannot be reduced to a reliable outreach sequence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing contact records, templates, suppression rules, and calendar workflows cover most supporting work. Small integrations can keep approved material current without a model loop.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding organisational needs, reaching the right person, and avoiding unsuitable promises depend on context and trust.
tasks.human_edge: Hear what the organisation actually needs and decide whether the service is suitable before pursuing a commercial next step.

ambition.what: A service-fit briefing for small regional associations, subject to confirming an unmet need.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time finding facts and entering repeated details, leaving more time for qualified conversations. No new pricing, capacity, or contracting rights are assumed.

reach.task: Define service segments and a clear value proposition.
reach.learn: Segmentation, service economics, and evidence for customer benefits.

reach.task: Create a reliable service and facility information sheet.
reach.learn: Structured content, factual ownership, accessibility, and version control.

evidence.claim: Lead management and configured communication journeys are available capabilities.
Approved templates, structured service facts, and contact rules can support outreach without autonomous agents.
Human conversations remain necessary for service fit, objections, and commitments.

assumptions: The typical task mixes contact selection, preparation, email, and live conversations; the exact channel mix varies.
Approved service facts can be stored as structured fields or consistently tagged documents.
Only configured rules and templates are needed for the initial version.
GDPR applies to identifiable business contacts, including the right to object to direct marketing [S14].
Marketing contact must follow applicable ePrivacy and national rules; business contact details alone do not establish permission [S12].
The live conversation is performed by the manager; separate approval gates apply to automated outbound sends.
Access ranges include permission-rule review and consultation under national rules if employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Which organisations are already customers, prospects, or suppressed contacts?
Which contact routes are permitted under the applicable national rules?
Who maintains service facts, facility availability, and commercial limits?
Does the existing contact system support suppression checks immediately before sending?
Are small regional associations an eligible group with an unmet service need?
Which proposed activity reports would expose individual employee performance?
research_questions: Which service-fit filters reduce irrelevant outreach without excluding suitable organisations?
Can approved templates handle common introductions without losing necessary context?
Where do contact permissions become stale between preparation and sending?
Which structured notes materially improve the next conversation?
new_work: Maintain service facts, template versions, and contact eligibility rules.
Review prepared messages and confirm requested follow-up before sending.
Synchronise objections and suppression status across contact channels.
Resolve incomplete contact records and failed appointment workflows.

role.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling campaign evidence and preparing routine material, and more time judging promotion economics, testing research methods, and building external relationships. Faster information supports more frequent recommendations; spending and commercial authority change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Market research analyst: design promotion holdouts and defensible samples.
Marketing manager: compare campaign contribution and define service segments.
Public relations manager: prepare association stakeholder positions.
Technical writer: maintain reliable service and facility information.
skills_to_grow: Campaign measurement, contribution margins, and causal inference.
Research design, neutral questionnaire wording, and pilot evaluation.
Structured content, data reconciliation, and exception management.
GDPR, permitted marketing contact, and applicable national rules.
Stakeholder listening and evidence-based commercial recommendations.
role.ambitious_version: Run a frequent promotion decision review supported by traceable costs and results, offer local teams pilot-tested research kits, and turn association conversations into reviewed member-needs briefings.
